computational_intent: Parse every JSON payload, propagating any parsing failure, and only after all parsing is complete return an exact Boolean indicating whether at least one record has a truthy active field and a key equal to the requested target.

contract_applicability.rationale: The contains_record loop is structurally an existence search over a finite list with the predicate bool(record["active"]) and record["key"] == target. Applicability remains unresolved because arbitrary parsed JSON values and Python truthiness/equality would need bounded reversible encodings, a coherent representation must be rebuilt for every batch, and no exact success/no-solution error policy or reversible oracle construction is supplied.

The program performs an existence test and defines neither a binary optimization objective nor constraints whose optimum is a required output. Recasting the Boolean search as a QUBO would add an optimization problem without preserving an evident computational purpose.

assumptions: Within the stated input domain, parsed records contain both key and active fields.
The required behavior includes parsing every payload before searching and propagating malformed-JSON exceptions.
The returned Boolean must preserve Python truthiness for active and Python equality against the string target.
risks: Every fresh batch requires classical parsing and at least linear-size data preparation before any coherent search representation could be used.
Oracle construction and coherent loading may cost as much as or more than the simple classical scan.
Grover-style measurement is probabilistic, while the software contract requires an exact Boolean and supplies no acceptable error threshold.
Encoding general JSON-derived values may require substantial workspace and reversible logic to reproduce Python truthiness and equality.
There is no scale information, benchmark evidence, approved cost model, coherent-memory facility, or evidence of end-to-end advantage.
Line 12 may be an expensive hotspot for large payloads, but it is a required classical parsing stage rather than a supported quantum search or optimization candidate.
rationale: Lines 4-8 admit an abstract Grover-style predicate-search formulation, so they are structurally eligible. They are not practically suitable under the supplied execution assumptions: all payloads must first be parsed even when an early record matches, malformed input must still raise, and a coherent representation must be constructed anew for every batch. Thus the complete operation retains unavoidable classical input work linear in the batch size, while the remaining predicate is a simple classical comparison. With no benchmark, scale, cost model, reusable oracle, or permitted probabilistic-error policy, no practical advantage or exact semantic preservation is established. The parsing comprehension is a potentially expensive but rejected hotspot because quantumizing it fits neither supported migration family and could violate required parsing effects.
